open_items.detail: Week 5 depends on published material the source does not contain: the Effective English comprehension passage and questions on page 152 (pages 152-153), the Standard Speech 10 Book, Diction in English Course, pages 2 to 6, pages 67 to 95 of Towards Effective Use of English by Folu Agoi, and questions 2 and 3 on page 205 of Effective English. Editions are not given.
open_items.required_action: Supply exact authorised extracts and editions, or have the owner accept labelled original equivalent activities (see ENGLISH-PRESCRIBED-PASSAGES). Until then none is taught as checked (queue item ENG-FACT-T3-W05-EXTERNAL-MATERIALS).

open_items.detail: Scheme row 5 names diphthongs /ei/ and /ai/ and conjuncts and disjuncts, but the Week 5 body teaches neither (its topics are scanning and skimming, the /f/-/v/, /s/-/z/ and /ʃ/-/ʒ/ contrasts, and nominalization). The 1st Term diphthong and adverb, conjunction and preposition lessons exist but are not bound to Week 5, and the scheme row and body disagree.
open_items.required_action: Owner to decide whether the 1st Term supplements are the intended Week 5 delivery or whether original Week 5 lessons are wanted; then author or bind accordingly with keyed, marked practice, labelled original (queue item ENG-LES-T3-W05-SCHEME-GAP). Do not infer content from the topic names.

open_items.detail: The skimming and scanning content has no passage, worked example or practice. The scanning explanation conflates scanning with previewing and with reading for main points, and the replacement reading lesson models the skills on an original passage without defining the method or keying a skimming task.
open_items.required_action: Author an original, labelled reading-skills lesson with a corrected definition of scanning, a short original passage and keyed, marked skimming and scanning questions, bound additively to SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-READING-T3 (queue item ENG-LES-T3-W05-READING-SKILLS). Do not infer the page 152 passage.

open_items.detail: The three sound-contrast tables have defects (proof/prove reversed, a repeated word and non-minimal pairs in /v/-/f/; one-in-four clean pairs and a pair with both words ending in /z/ in /s/-/z/; reversed /ʒ/ and /ʃ/ columns), and no practice is keyed. Correction COR-018 replaces the whole of ENGLISH-BODY-071 with SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-PHONETICS-T3, which names the voicing pairs and the column-reversal fact but has no word lists or contrast practice. The replacement does not teach the nominalization half of the row, so the row-level IMPLEMENTED_EQUIVALENT of ENGLISH-BODY-071 overstates its scope; that status is left unchanged here and the downgrade is left to the owner, as for ENGLISH-BODY-021.
open_items.required_action: Author original, dictionary-checked minimal-pair lists with transcription for /f/-/v/, /s/-/z/ and /ʃ/-/ʒ/ and a keyed, marked contrast practice, labelled original, bound additively to SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-PHONETICS-T3 (queue item ENG-LES-T3-W05-SOUND-CONTRASTS). Oral production stays a teacher observation, not a written key.

open_items.detail: The nominalization content is partly covered by the 1st Term noun and 3rd Term affix supplements (-ment, -ness, -ity, and the plural of compound nouns) but not the definition, the definite article plus an adjective, the infix claim, the -hood claim about adverbs, the garbled suffix list, the second compound-noun table (talisman and linguafranca are not compounds, highway man) or man friend. The task of forming nouns from phaty, tis and the other affixes has no key.
open_items.required_action: Author an original, labelled nominalization lesson (definition, affixation, the + adjective, conversion, and a corrected suffix list with examples) with a keyed, marked practice on forming nouns, bound additively to SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-AFFIXES-T3 and SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-NOUNS-T1 (queue item ENG-LES-T3-W05-NOMINALIZATION). Do not repair the source lists in place.

open_items.detail: The Week 6 affixes replacement SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-AFFIXES-T3 is narrower than the source body: it teaches selected prefixes, one harmless example, and -ed/-ing patterns, but not the full source prefix inventory, the -less negation examples, or the source's -en/-ze tense-form examples. The source itself has apparent gloss/wording defects (including ante/anti, “unn”, “arch” and “-ze”), which are recorded, not silently repaired. Plural -ies/-es is separately covered by SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-NOUNS-T1. The body-level IMPLEMENTED_EQUIVALENT status of ENGLISH-BODY-072 therefore overstates the complete row's objective-level coverage.
open_items.required_action: Owner/coordinator to decide whether ENGLISH-BODY-072 and COR-019 should retain row-level IMPLEMENTED_EQUIVALENT status. Complete the uncovered Week 6 affix objectives with accurate, source-aware original teaching and keyed, marked practice; confirm the intended treatment of the source's “-ze” rather than normalising it silently.

open_items.detail: The source's two-syllable stress strand includes a first-syllable list, a prefix-related second-syllable exception with ten examples, four noun/verb pairs, and a seven-word evaluation. SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-STRESS-T3 explains word stress and gives a record/reCORD contrast, but does not preserve these source-specific lists, exception examples or evaluation. The body-level IMPLEMENTED_EQUIVALENT status of ENGLISH-BODY-073 therefore overstates the objective-level coverage.
open_items.required_action: Owner/coordinator to decide whether ENGLISH-BODY-073 and COR-020 should retain row-level IMPLEMENTED_EQUIVALENT status. Expand the same-term stress teaching to cover the missing source objectives with checked examples and keyed, marked practice; keep oral/listening verification separate.

open_items.detail: The Week 6 source explains narrative sequence, climax and past-tense use and gives the specific “It is a man’s world” prompt. SUP-SS1-ENGLISH-ESSAY-REPORT-T1 provides generic narrative planning, but neither it nor the source row supplies a worked outline/model for this prompt or a specific marking rubric.
open_items.required_action: Author an original same-term story-writing supplement with a worked plan or model, consistent narrative tense, a task on the source prompt and a transparent writing rubric. Label new teaching as original and do not invent a source model.

open_items.detail: Week 6 refers to external reading material not included in the source archive: Complete English Course, pages 420-423; Standard Speech 10 Book, Diction in English Course, page 23; and Countdown WASSCE/SSCE English Language by Evans, pages 5-7. The source gives no editions and none of these extracts is supplied.
open_items.required_action: Owner to supply authorised extracts and editions for the three assignments, or accept clearly labelled original equivalent activities. Do not infer the missing textbook content.

open_items.detail: The Week 6 weekend assignment contains five vocabulary multiple-choice items, five nearest-in-meaning items and five article/determiner choices, but no answer key or marks. Several stems/options are garbled or ambiguous; no answer can safely be inferred from option position.
open_items.required_action: Owner/teacher to supply an authoritative key and marking allocation, or author a labelled original parallel revision set with defensible items, keyed answers and a complete marking breakdown. Do not invent a key for the defective source exercise.
